# Adversarial Review Synthesis — Waves −1 and 0

## 1. WAVE −1 VERDICT — **COMMIT AFTER LISTED FIXES** (do not deploy until B1–B2 land)

Both reviewers independently reproduced the same blocker by executing the `make -n deploy` payload against a stubbed `docker`, and both confirm the mitigations themselves are sound (`.env` still syncs, guards fire and pass correctly across an 11-case matrix, eval anchor protected, 555 tests green). Nothing here warrants rejection; the deploy recipe is a bad six lines inside an otherwise good change. Neither reviewer executed anything against the live host.

**Blockers (must land before the next `make deploy`)**

| # | Where | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `Makefile:214-220` (deploy ssh payload) | `&&` chain severed by `;` after `built=$(...)`. A **failed** `docker compose build` no longer aborts: `built` falls back to stale `fp-gcf:latest`, that stale image is tagged with the **new** sha, `docker compose up -d` recreates production on old code, `docker compose ps` returns 0, make prints `deployed fp-gcf:<sha>`. Regression — the pre-change pure-`&&` chain exited 1. Also poisons the rollback tag namespace the same wave creates. Reproduced by both reviewers (exit 0 held vs exit 1 parent). | Replace both `;` with `&&`; prefix the remote payload with `set -e`; delete the `:latest` fallback in favour of a hard failure. |
| B2 | `Makefile:215-218` (`--images` probe + `:latest` fallback) | The fallback is correct only for the **old** compose spelling. Under `docker-compose.yaml:56` `image: fp-gcf:${GIT_SHA:-latest}` (landing in this same wave), a **successful** build produces `fp-gcf:<sha>`; if the probe returns empty (stderr swallowed by `2>/dev/null`; old compose, interpolation error, bad remote `.env`), `docker tag fp-gcf:latest fp-gcf:<sha>` overwrites the fresh sha tag with a stale image and `up -d` starts it. Exit 0, reported as a new-sha deploy. Shell consequence reproduced; premise (probe failing on the remote) unverified against the live host. | Resolve deterministically from the already-exported `GIT_SHA` (`docker image inspect $(IMAGE):$(GIT_SHA)`), stop swallowing stderr, no `:latest` guess. |

**Land in the same pass (both reviewers, confirmed):** `docs/DEPLOYED.md:28-29` claims rows are auto-appended by `deploy` — `grep -n DEPLOYED Makefile` finds only a comment at :110, so the incident-time artifact ships permanently empty while asserting it is maintained (and if the append is added it dirties the tree, colliding with `_check-clean-tree`). `Makefile:111` `GIT_SHA ?=` lets the environment stamp production images and rollback tags (`GIT_SHA=deadbee make -n deploy` proves it) — the exact footgun this wave fixed for `NAME`, left on the one variable that names what runs in production, and the new compose header actively tells operators to `export GIT_SHA`.

**Also confirmed, non-blocking:** `docs/claim-support-execution-plan.md:397` prescribes an ssh-side `.env` edit "never by rsync — `.env` is excluded", which is false; rsync silently reverts the Wave-5 flip and `FLIP=1` becomes a no-op. `_check-clean-tree` outside a git checkout prints a git usage dump plus a false "working tree is dirty" with an empty change list. `data/registry*.json` was dropped from the plan's exclude list without disclosure (1.2 MB of load-bearing planner input, still ships every push). Unreadable `.env` fails the repair guard **open**. `VERIFY_REPAIR=1` followed by `VERIFY_REPAIR=0` false-alarms (last-wins not evaluated). `preflight`/`deploy` say "HEAD `<sha>`" when push ships the working tree plus `.env` and 1.4 GB of gitignored index. Guards bypassable via `make -o _check-clean-tree -o _check-repair-flag push` (undisclosed) and via environment-set `ALLOW_DIRTY`/`FLIP`. Untracked-file list silently truncates at 20.

## 2. WAVE 0 VERDICT on `hold/verifier-calibration` — **NEEDS REWORK, NOT MERGEABLE**

All four subject reviewers returned REFUTED / DO-NOT-DEPLOY, on four independent surfaces. Two of the four hard repair gates are defeated **behaviourally**, both headline metrics of the "split" are wrong, the adjudication tool cannot support the labelling task it exists for, and the test suite does not pin the changes. This is not a fix list against a sound design — the metric definitions, the entity matcher, and the export schema each need re-specifying. **Do not flip `VERIFY_REPAIR=1`.** Note the wave also regresses the **live** `VERIFY=1 / VERIFY_REPAIR=0` production path, so it is not merely a pre-flip concern.

### CONFIRMED — blocker

1. **`verify.py:1129-1131` + `:1086-1102` — GATE 1 defeated (two-field sentence).** `_field_conflict` derives stated figures from `_field_context_amounts` and returns `None` when it is empty; the slicing drops any amount before the field label, so any two-label sentence yields `[]` and the contradiction test short-circuits. `classify_deterministic:1451-1452` gates `registry_conflict` on the same empty list. A repair reporting the total-financing figure as GCF financing re-verifies `supported` and is **adopted** (parent rejects it). Also flips CONTRADICTED→SUPPORTED live today.
2. **`verify.py:1155-1156` + `:1075-1083` — GATE 1 defeated (chained bracket).** `_citation_context` requires `len(cited) == 1`, so `[docA, p.45; docB, p.5]` yields `""` for **every** document; `_scoped_field_conflict` then `continue`s past all of them. Widening a bracket flips the identical FP172 sentence from CONTRADICTED (known-document-conflict, 21,128,224 p.6 vs 49,151,817 p.76) to SUPPORTED with an **empty flags list**. 13 chained brackets already sit in the 66 recorded answers, concentrated in the comparison/conflict classes. Inherited block citations hit the same hole. Fails **open** — invisible to any pass-rate metric.
3. **`verify.py:554-568` `_entity_present` — GATE 3 precondition emptied, correct answers flagged.** On real recorded traffic, 4 entity variants flip supported→unsupported and `id-fp173-entity` goes **verified → ABSTAIN** ("FP173 is implemented by the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB)" — correct, correctly cited). Because `_supported_required(verdicts)` drops to 0, the anti-gutting gate at `:1929` never runs and a bare refusal can replace a mostly-correct answer.
4. **`eval_answers.py:582,595-596` — `citation_completeness` counts any bracket, not "cited AND supported".** A fabricated citation to a never-retrieved document scores 1.0. On release-1: reported 141/165 = 85.5% vs the contract's 91/165 = 55.2% — a 30-point inflation on the metric the ≥95% acceptance gate is scored against, trivially gamed by appending `[anything, p.1]`.
5. **`verify.py:1417-1423` + `eval_answers.py:580-581` — groundedness is not computed over all held evidence.** `value-present-elsewhere` is set only on the `if not c.citations` branch, so for cited claims groundedness collapses onto citation-support and the split carries zero independent information exactly where miscitation lives. Non-monotone: **deleting** a citation raises groundedness (18 of 66 answers). Produces 50 "citation-complete but not grounded" claims. Binding decision 3 assigns this rescoping to this wave; none of wave 0b's other listed files were touched.
6. **`scripts/adjudicate_claims.py:25-38,131-141` — the export drops every piece of evidence the labels are defined over.** `claims.evidence_keys` (71/71), `hits`, `notes_used.registry` (58/71) all omitted. For the 24/71 claims whose entire signal is "no citation on a factual claim", `missing_citation` vs `missing_retrieval_evidence` vs `verifier_false_positive` is undecidable from the row. The companion `scripts/backfill_release_evidence.py` is not in the wave.

## 4. WHERE THE REVIEWERS DISAGREED

- **Wave −1 landing strategy.** Reviewer 1: ship Task C (eval anchor) now, **hold** Task A's deploy/rollback targets and keep Task B's compose change from landing ahead of them, because the new `${GIT_SHA:-latest}` spelling is what turns B2 from harmless into a stale-code deploy. Reviewer 2: fix the two deploy-chain findings and land everything in the same pass. Not resolved here — R1's sequencing is safer if the fixes slip; R2's is simpler if they don't.
- **What actually breaks `_entity_present` on real data.** The gates reviewer attributes the damage to `_contains_norm`'s word-boundary tightening (possessive/slash forms; 592 of 1771 acronym-bearing corpus chunks print the acronym only possessively) and treats it as a false-positive generator. The live-path reviewer measured the recorded 66 answers and reports **4 alias-driven regressions and 0 word-boundary-only regressions**, attributing the damage entirely to the `_claimed_alias` short-circuit rejecting long-form-only evidence. The tests reviewer confirms `_contains_norm` does flip a real verdict ('Ministry of Environment' vs 'Ministry of Environmental Protection') but frames that flip as a **desirable** tightening that is merely unpinned. Both halves need work; which is the priority is unsettled, and whether the word-boundary change is a bug or an improvement is a genuine open question.
- **`_check_existence` — regression or fix?** The metrics reviewer classes the `bc-b42-02-add16` demotion as "a false-positive fix, though it does create a new false-negative surface". The live-path reviewer classes the same change as a fail-closed regression and asks for the parent's fail-open default to be restored. Decide deliberately; do not let it land undecided.
- **"Was the matcher relaxed?"** The metrics reviewer's headline is that **no matcher was relaxed** — net 3 claims **tighter** over release-1 (4 demotions, 1 correct promotion) — so the inflated metrics come entirely from the definitions. The gates and live-path reviewers demonstrate a real relaxation in the conflict path (chained bracket: CONTRADICTED → SUPPORTED). These are reconcilable but must be stated together: the relaxation does not fire on the recorded answers **as recorded**, only when a bracket is widened — which is exactly what a repair pass can do, and there are already 13 chained brackets in the set.
- **Can deterministic mode make an API call?** The metrics reviewer lists "`--verifier-mode deterministic` (the default) cannot make an extra API call" as **clean**, correctly conditioned on default flags. The tests reviewer shows the parser accepts `--verifier-mode deterministic --verifier-repair` and that combination makes a real call. Both are true; the clean finding should be read as scoped to the default invocation only.
- **Severity of `docs/DEPLOYED.md`.** Reviewer 1 rated it high ("the artifact ships making a false claim about the system"); reviewer 2 rated it medium. Same finding, same fix.
- **Coverage asymmetry, not conflict.** Only Reviewer 1 examined rollback's `:latest` handling (medium, `confirmed:false` — docker unavailable, live host off-limits) and the non-git-checkout guard failure. Only Reviewer 2 examined the execution-plan flip procedure and the dropped `data/registry*.json` exclude. Neither contradicts the other; neither was independently re-checked.
